title: Equinox Gold Reports Q3 Results; Transformational Combination Begins to Deliver
summary: Equinox Gold reports third quarter financial and operating results, achieves record revenue and adjusted EBITDA following combination with Orla Mining.

Released on


November 9, 2026


# Equinox Gold Reports Q3 Results; Transformational Combination Begins to Deliver


[Download](https://www.equinoxgold.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/20261109-EQX-Q3-2026-Results-News-Release-Final-draft.pdf)


***Record Quarterly Revenue of $1.0 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $533.0 million***


Equinox Gold Corp. (TSX: EQX, NYSE American: EQX) (“Equinox Gold” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce its financial and operating results for the third quarter of 2026 (“Q3 2026”). *All dollar figures are in United States dollars unless otherwise noted* .


**Third Quarter 2026 Summary:** ****


- **Gold production and sales:** Produced 237,019 ounces and sold 248,484 ounces at an average realized gold price of $4,157 per ounce, generating record revenue of $1.0 billion. Q3 2026 production and sales include two months of attributable production from Musselwhite (Canada) and Camino Rojo (Mexico) following the closing of the business combination with Orla Mining Ltd. (“Orla”) on July 31, 2026.
- **Costs:** Cash costs were $1,654 and all-in sustaining costs (“AISC”) were $2,091 per ounce of gold sold1 , representing a decrease of 9% and 4%, respectively, compared to Q2 2026.
- **Guidance:** The Company remains on track to meet the low end of the updated annual production guidance range of 870,000 to 920,000 ounces and the high end of the AISC guidance range of $1,900 to $2,000 per ounce of gold sold.
- **Record quarterly adjusted EBITDA:** Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter totaled $533.0 million1 , an increase of 49% compared to Q2 2026, and included the contribution from the first two months of ownership of Musselwhite and Camino Rojo.
- **Net income:** Net income for the quarter was $62.5 million, or $0.06 per share, and adjusted net income was $199.3 million, or $0.19 per share1 .
- **Cash flow:** Cash flow from operations before changes in non-cash working capital of $291.7 million, and mine-site free cash flow before changes in working capital of $398.3 million.
- **Balance sheet strength:** The Company ended the quarter with $527.9 million of unrestricted cash and cash equivalents. Net cash at quarter end, excluding the 2023 convertible notes that were redeemed subsequent to quarter end, was $164.0 million, and liquidity was $1.2 billion1 ,2 .
- **Leadership transition:** On July 31, 2026, the Company announced that Darren Hall would retire as Chief Executive Officer and Director of Equinox Gold, effective October 31, 2026. Jason Simpson assumed the role of President and Chief Executive Officer on November 1, 2026.
- **Continued return of capital to shareholders:** Returned $35.3 million to shareholders during Q3 2026 through $9.0 million of share repurchases and $26.3 million of cash dividends. Year-to-date, as of November 6, 2026, the Company has repurchased 2,370,200 shares for approximately $27.7 million and paid $50.0 million in dividends. The dividend was increased by 50% in August 2026 to $0.09 per share annually.


**Jason Simpson, President and Chief Executive Officer of Equinox Gold, commented:** “This quarter’s results are only a partial reflection of the transformation of Equinox Gold into an emerging senior gold producer following the completion of our combination with Orla partway through the quarter. Valentine increased gold production by 6% this quarter, supported by a 16% increase in mill feed grade that averaged over 1.8 g/t, and achieved September mill throughput 26% above nameplate capacity. Our operating priority as a leading Canadian gold producer is to translate progress at Valentine and Greenstone combined with Musselwhite into consistent production and stronger cash generation. We are on track to exceed one million gold ounces produced on a combined twelve-month basis, securing our position among senior producers. During the quarter, we commenced construction activities at South Railroad following the receipt of the Federal Record of Decision in August. South Railroad is set to become our next new mine with first gold targeted in the first half of 2028, and production averaging 130,000 ounces per year over the first five years of an initial 10 year mine life.”


“Our strong financial position and cash flow generation provide Equinox Gold with the flexibility to advance organic growth in a disciplined manner while continuing to return capital to shareholders. We remain confident in Equinox Gold’s long-term outlook, focused on operational execution and advancing our internally funded North American growth strategy to deliver lasting long-term value per share.”

**Operational Review** ****


**Greenstone** produced 60,596 ounces and operations continue to improve as the mine moves through the final stages of ramp-up, with a focus on consistent throughput and mill availability. In Q3, mining rates averaged approximately 194,000 tonnes per day (“tpd”). Scheduled replacement of the high-pressure grinding rolls in August 2026 reduced plant throughput during the quarter to an average of 23,682 tpd. Greenstone is positioned for stronger production through the remainder of 2026, with further operational improvements expected to support consistent performance over the longer term. Commissioning of the trommel (now onsite), which is expected to improve mill availability by removing timber and metal from the mill feed, is planned for early 2027.


**Musselwhite** produced 63,090 ounces during the quarter, exceeding expectations due to higher tonnes processed. Of this production, 45,616 ounces were attributable to Equinox Gold for the period from July 31 to September 30, 2026. Development of the 1080 exploration drift and underground drilling continue to support near-term production and longer-term reserve and resource growth.


**Valentine** produced 34,719 ounces, up 6% from Q2 2026, driven mainly by a 16% increase in processed grade to over 1.8 g/t, as mining initiatives including selective mining practices continued to improve. Average daily mining rates were 6% higher compared to the prior quarter and increased further to an average of 132,000 tpd in October 2026. The mill achieved throughput of 8,650 tpd in September, exceeding nameplate capacity by 26%, following a planned maintenance shutdown in August. In September, the mine produced 14,027 ounces, its highest monthly total since operations began in September 2025.


**Nicaragua Operations** produced 58,489 ounces with consistent average gold grade processed compared to the previous quarter. Near-term activities remain focused on developing future ore sources, with planned waste stripping continuing during the quarter.


**Camino Rojo** produced 26,168 ounces during the quarter of which 18,975 ounces were attributable to Equinox Gold from July 31 to September 30, 2026. Gold recovery was lower during the quarter, as anticipated, as mining progressed through transitional ore. The leach pad expansion was completed in October 2026 with stacking and leaching activities underway in the new area.


**Mesquite** produced 17,116 ounces. Following a geotechnical instability in the Brownie Phase 4 area in Q3 2026, the team is focused on mine sequencing to optimize short term production and continues to assess mine-life extension opportunities.


**Development Projects**


**Valentine Phase 2 Expansion, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada**


The Valentine Phase 2 expansion is expected to increase processing throughput from approximately 2.5 million tonnes per year to 5.0 million tonnes per year. On August 5, 2026, the Board approved construction with an initial capital budget of $436 million, including $54 million of contingency. During Q3 2026, detailed engineering advanced and orders were placed for key long-lead items, including an additional ball mill, gyratory crusher and tailings thickener. The Company also submitted an application to Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro to proceed with a full impact study for the additional power requirements associated with the Phase 2 expansion. Construction is expected to be completed in late 2028.


Growth capital expenditures were $8.3 million during Q3 2026.


**South Railroad Project, Nevada, U.S.**


South Railroad is a planned open-pit, heap-leach operation on the Carlin Trend in Nevada, U.S. Following receipt of the federal Record of Decision on August 14, 2026, the Company commenced early works construction activities. At September 30, 2026, detailed engineering was 71% complete and approximately $180 million of the estimated $395 million initial capital had been committed. Long-lead procurement advanced for the ADR (adsorption, desorption and recovery) plant, crushing systems and site power generators. Mining equipment is expected to begin arriving at site at the end of 2026, and initial mining is planned for spring 2027 with first gold production targeted for the first half of 2028.


Growth capital expenditures from July 31 to September 30, 2026 were $20.1 million. Remaining key state permits and water rights are expected through the end of 2026 and into 2027. **** ****

**Liquidity and Capital Allocation** ****


At September 30, 2026, Equinox Gold had $527.9 million of unrestricted cash and cash equivalents and $512.0 million of total debt resulting in net cash, excluding the 2023 convertible notes that were redeemed subsequent to quarter end, of $164.0 million. Available liquidity of $1.2 billion includes unrestricted cash and cash equivalents at the end of the quarter, plus $634.6 million of undrawn amount under the revolving credit facility at September 30, 2026.


During the first nine months of 2026, the Company made $1.3 billion of total debt repayments, including repayment of the term loan, Sprott loan, amounts under the revolving credit facility and debt assumed in the Orla business combination.


Subsequent to quarter end, all outstanding 2023 convertible notes, with an aggregate principal amount of $172.5 million, were converted into 28,475,117 common shares.


**Continued return of capital to shareholders:**


- During the quarter, the Company repurchased 759,000 shares at a cost of approximately $9.0 million under its normal course issuer bid. Year-to-date, as of November 6, 2026, the Company has repurchased 2,370,200 shares at a total cost of approximately $27.7 million.
- Paid cash dividends of $26.3 million, or $0.0225 per share, on September 2, 2026. In August 2026, the Company’s dividend was raised by 50%, from an annualized dividend of $0.06 to $0.09 per share. Year-to-date the Company has distributed $50.0 million in cash dividends to shareholders.
- On November 9, 2026, the Board of Directors approved a quarterly dividend of $0.0225 per share to be paid on December 10, 2026 to shareholders of record at the close of business on November 25, 2026.

**Non-IFRS Measures**


In this news release, cash costs, cash costs per oz sold, AISC, AISC per oz sold, adjusted net income, adjusted EPS, mine-site free cash flow, adjusted EBITDA, net debt, and sustaining capital expenditures are measures with no standardized meaning under IFRS, i.e. they are non-IFRS measures, and may not be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. Their measurement and presentation is consistently prepared and is intended to provide additional information and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for measures of performance prepared in accordance with IFRS. Numbers presented in the tables below may not sum due to rounding.


**Cash Costs and Cash Costs per oz Sold**


Cash costs is a common financial performance measure in the gold mining industry; however, it has no standard meaning under IFRS. The Company reports total cash costs on a per oz sold basis. The Company believes that, in addition to conventional measures prepared in accordance with IFRS, certain investors use this information to evaluate the Company’s performance and ability to generate operating income and cash flow from mining operations. Cash costs are calculated as mine site operating costs and are net of costs allocated to by-products. Cash costs are divided by ounces sold to arrive at cash costs per oz sold. In calculating cash costs, the Company deducts costs allocated to by-products as it considers the cost to produce the gold is reduced as a result of the by-product sales incidental to the gold production process, thereby allowing management and other stakeholders to assess the net costs of gold production. The measure is not necessarily indicative of cash flow from operations under IFRS or operating costs presented under IFRS.


**AISC per oz Sold**


The Company uses AISC per oz of gold sold to measure performance. The methodology for calculating AISC was developed internally and is outlined below. Current IFRS measures used in the gold industry, such as operating expenses, do not capture all of the expenditures incurred to discover, develop and sustain gold production. The Company believes AISC per oz sold provides further transparency into costs associated with producing gold and will assist analysts, investors and other stakeholders of the Company in assessing its operating performance, its ability to generate free cash flow from current operations and its overall value. AISC includes cash costs (described above) and also includes sustaining capital expenditures, sustaining lease payments, reclamation cost accretion and amortization and exploration and evaluation costs. This measure seeks to reflect the full cost of gold production from current operations, therefore, expansionary capital and non-sustaining expenditures are excluded.
